role: Index of ADRs 001-006 with inline summaries of 001 (encryption fallback), 002 (CI cost posture), 003 (concurrency allowlist) and pointers to 004-006.

units.does: Index table mapping ADR 001-006 to where reasoning lives (PendingEncryptionLedger.swift, CI_POSTURE.md, check_unchecked_sendable.sh, adr files). All linked files exist.

flags.text: ADR 001 says the plaintext window 'is bounded by one app launch'; reencryptPendingSessions returns early (keeps the ledger) when the key is still unavailable, and reencryptOne leaves a session queued when its read fails (e.g. a locked background launch), so plaintext can persist across several launches; the stated bound is not guaranteed.

ADR 001 says the fallback window 'is logged at .error'; the common fallback (encryptionManager unavailable before first unlock) calls onFailure() and returns nil with no log, and archiveWriteOptions records the ledger silently. Only an encrypt() throw, or a launch where the key is still unavailable, logs at .error; the normal fallback goes unlogged.

ADR 002 says the script gates run 'on a Linux runner on every push'; gates.yml triggers on push to main only (plus pull_request and workflow_dispatch), so pushes to other branches with no PR run no gates.

units.key: § Architecture decision records > 001 — Sensitive storage falls back, then repairs
units.does: Claims: when EncryptionManager is unavailable (before first unlock), archive writes plaintext with .completeFileProtection, records the session in PendingEncryptionLedger, and reencryptPendingSessions() rewrites it encrypted at the next launch where the key is reachable; the window is 'bounded by one app launch'; only a throwing encrypt() is logged at .error, while the key-unavailable fallback is not logged and shows only as the ledger entry. Verified the write options (Archive+PendingEncryption.swift:18-30), encryptOrReportFailure (Archive+SessionCodec.swift:113-126: isAvailable guard returns nil silently, catch logs .error), and the launch-time repair called from ArchiveMigrations.runDeferredMigrations.

flags.text: ADR says the plaintext window is 'bounded by one app launch', but reencryptPendingSessions returns early (leaving entries queued) when the key is still unavailable at launch, and pendingSession defers when the file is unreadable (background launch while locked), so the window spans any number of launches.

units.key: § Architecture decision records > 002 — Nothing that needs macOS runs automatically
units.does: Claims macOS jobs stay manual (10x billing, ~1,080 billable minutes per full run vs 3,000 cap) and script gates run on a Linux runner on every push via gates.yml. Verified: gates.yml triggers on push to main, pull_request, workflow_dispatch; CI_POSTURE.md:24-30 carries the arithmetic.

units.key: § Architecture decision records > 003 — Concurrency escapes are allowlisted, not eliminated
units.does: Claims remaining @unchecked Sendable / nonisolated(unsafe) annotations are in allowlisted files, count read from .ci/unchecked_sendable_budget.txt (14), enforced by check_unchecked_sendable.sh. Verified: 14 allowlisted files, 14 non-comment annotations.

flags.text: ADR says each allowlisted escape names the queue/lock/contract that owns its state and the count is 'stated nowhere else', but check_unchecked_sendable.sh:106-118 still justifies escapes in SettingsManager.swift:16, LanguageManager.swift:35/47 and RRCollector.swift:303 that no longer exist in the tree (the grep finds no annotation in those files).

units.key: § Architecture decision records > 004 — Debt is ratcheted, never waived
§ Architecture decision records > 005 — Helpers hold their owner strongly; `unowned` is banned
units.does: Summary of ADR 005: 28 helpers had unowned back-pointers and 'two of them crashed the unit suite from resumed continuations'; they are now values holding the owner strongly, built on demand, and a gate bans unowned. Consistent with ADR 005, which says the crash reports named two sites (005-no-unowned-back-references.md:66); the 'unit suite' wording omits that the first reproduction was in four observable-state tests (005:64).
